content:
I recently tried out a range of new MagSafe wallets and noticed that these products are increasingly resembling traditional wallets. The one I tried most recently is the Vinich MagSafe wallet, which comes in over 15 colour options. It looks like a traditional bifold wallet, and its design won't clash at all with a leather iPhone case — it really feels like an extension of your iPhone case.

MagSafe Monday column: Every Monday, Bradley Chambers breaks down the latest developments in MagSafe and the wireless charging industry, helping you get the most out of your wireless charging-enabled Apple devices.

Colour options

The manufacturer has clearly put a lot of effort into colours, offering black, green, brown, and even purple — all with a vintage, weathered look that won't clash with leather cases but instead complements them quite harmoniously. Beyond these, there are countless other colours to choose from. Vinich also offers a "Desert Titanium" colourway; if you don't like using a case, this colour matches your iPhone perfectly.

Wallet capacity

Vinich advertises three card slots and notes that, depending on card thickness, it can actually hold three to five cards. For everyday use, one driver's licence, two or three credit cards, and a company access card are basically sufficient. Behind the card slots, there's also space to fold and tuck away a few banknotes. For such a compact wallet, I find it surprisingly practical — I usually carry around about US$20 in cash.

The card slots are lined with RFID-blocking material, and the entire interior is lined with microfibre so your cards won't constantly rub against the fabric. The magnetic strength is moderate — I've used ones with stronger magnets and ones with much weaker ones.

Three things you should know before buying

First, this is made of synthetic leather, not genuine leather. It has scratch resistance and reinforced stitching, which is reasonable at this price point, but if you're planning to pair it with a genuine leather case, be aware that the two materials may not match perfectly. Vinich recommends caring for the wallet every three to six months.

Second, when taking ultrawide or macro photos, the wallet may gradually drift into the camera's field of view. Most iPhone wallets sit below the camera, but if you're shooting close-up detail shots, it's best to remove it to make sure it doesn't cover the lens at all.

Finally, it can't be used as a stand, even though it might look like it could. The cover is intentionally designed to be relatively soft to reduce pressure on the MagSafe ring, so if you're looking for a wallet that can prop up your iPhone for hands-free calls or video watching, this one isn't for you.

Conclusion

At under US$25, the colour options alone are worth a look, especially if you've been looking for a style that pairs perfectly with a beautiful leather case. Most MagSafe wallets are designed to be as understated as possible, but this one is designed to complement your case — both in feel and appearance, it still feels like a traditional wallet that can be used on its own. It would be even better if Find My tracking could be added in the future.

You can purchase this Vinich MagSafe wallet directly from Amazon or the Vinich website.
